sources.title: ReHLDS engine sv_main.cpp - SV_BanId_f, Host_Kick_f, SV_RemoveId_f, SV_WriteId_f, SV_Rcon
ReHLDS engine host_cmd.cpp - Host_Status_f output format
Essential RCON Commands Every CS 1.6 Admin Needs

notes: CS 1.6 runs on the GoldSrc Half-Life Dedicated Server (SteamCMD app 90, mod dir 'cstrike'). RCON is NOT Source RCON: it is a connectionless UDP text protocol on the same UDP port as the game (default 27015), preceded by a 'challenge rcon' handshake, then '\xFF\xFF\xFF\xFFrcon <challenge> <password> <command>' - SV_Rcon/SV_Rcon_Validate in sv_main.cpp read Cmd_Argv(1) as the challenge and Cmd_Argv(2) as the password - hence flavour 'custom'. There is no separate RCON port or enable switch: setting the rcon_password cvar (usually in cstrike/server.cfg) turns RCON on, and the port is the server port set with -port/+port. Command text is taken from the engine's own usage strings: 'Usage:  banid <minutes> <uniqueid or #userid> { kick }' with 'Use 0 minutes for permanent', 'usage:  kick < name > | < # userid > [reason]', 'Usage:  removeid <uniqueid | #slotnumber>'. Pass {duration} in MINUTES and 0 for permanent. COM_Parse emits ':' as its own token, so a Steam ID arrives split across several argv slots: Host_Kick_f reassembles it as Cmd_Argv(2):Cmd_Argv(4):Cmd_Argv(6) only when the id follows a bare '#' ('kick # STEAM_0:1:12345678'), and then skips 4 extra tokens to find the reason; a Steam ID with no '#' is compared against player NAMES and matches nobody. SV_BanId_f and SV_RemoveId_f reassemble the same way and need no '#' (banid accepts at most 8 argv slots, which 'banid 0 <steamid> kick' exactly fills; the '#' in removeid is a ban-list SLOT number, not a userid). Bans are in-memory until 'writeid' is run. writeid REWRITES the file named by the bannedcfgfile cvar (default banned.cfg, i.e. cstrike/banned.cfg) from scratch - it opens it "wt" and is not an append - and it emits ONLY permanent entries, as 'banid 0.0 STEAM_0:1:12345678' lines; a ban with {duration} greater than 0 is never persisted and dies with the server, so only 'banid 0 <id> kick' survives a restart. IP bans go to listipcfgfile (default listip.cfg) via addip/writeip and are not covered here. A durable ban is 'banid 0 <id> kick' then 'writeid', a durable unban is 'removeid <id>' then 'writeid' - the schema allows one command string per field, so the follow-up writeid must be issued separately. No MOTD command exists; the MOTD is the file named by the motdfile cvar (default motd.txt). status output is 'hostname/version/tcp-ip/map/players' then the header '#      name userid uniqueid frag time ping loss adr' and one '#%2i %8s %i %s' row per client, the %8s being the name wrapped in quotes - which is what linePattern matches; fakeclients print 'BOT' instead of a Steam ID and are therefore skipped. DISAGREEMENT: several hosting knowledge bases (e.g. gamesclan.net) list 'rcon ban <player name or STEAM id>'; there is no 'ban' command in GoldSrc - that entry is wrong. Commands listed here are vanilla engine commands; AMX Mod X (amx_kick, amx_ban) is a plugin and is not assumed. Confidence 'high': the engine source and an independent community reference agree on status, banid, removeid, writeid and say. The kick-by-SteamID form rests on the engine source alone - the community page shows only 'kick #<userid>' and 'kick "<name>"' - but it was read directly out of Host_Kick_f rather than inferred.
